title: Counit-normalized comparison with an arbitrary right adjoint on fixed pairs
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories, $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ and $P:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D$ endofunctors, and $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ left adjoint to $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$, with counit $\varepsilon:FG\to\mathrm{id}$. Use the fixed-pair categories of [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]: an object of $\mathcal C^Q$ is $(M,\theta_M:QM\xrightarrow{\sim}M)$, and its morphisms $v$ satisfy $v\theta_M=\theta_NQ(v)$; similarly for $\mathcal D^P$. All composition in the following formulas is ordinary right-to-left composition. Let $\beta:PF\xrightarrow{\sim}FQ$ be a natural isomorphism and let $e:QG\xrightarrow{\sim}GP$ be its inverse's adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], so that
$$\varepsilon_{PK}\circ F(e_K)=P(\varepsilon_K)\circ\beta_{GK}^{-1}.$$
Let $\widetilde F:\mathcal C^Q\to\mathcal D^P$ send $(M,\theta_M)$ to $(FM,F(\theta_M)\beta_M)$ and act as $F$ on carrier morphisms. Suppose $\widetilde G:\mathcal D^P\to\mathcal C^Q$ is a right adjoint to $\widetilde F$, its carrier functor is $G$, and its adjunction counit has carrier $\varepsilon_K$ at every fixed pair $(K,\theta)$. Write $\vartheta_{K,\theta}:QGK\xrightarrow{\sim}GK$ for the structure of $\widetilde G(K,\theta)$. Then
$$\vartheta_{K,\theta}=G(\theta)\circ e_K.$$
For every other right adjoint $J$ of $\widetilde F$, with counit $\kappa$, there is a unique counit-compatible natural isomorphism $\alpha:J\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde G$. At each $(K,\theta)$ its carrier satisfies
$$\varepsilon_K\circ F(\operatorname{For}(\alpha_{K,\theta}))=\operatorname{For}(\kappa_{K,\theta}).$$
Thus $J(K,\theta)$ is canonically isomorphic in $\mathcal C^Q$ to $(GK,G(\theta)e_K)$, without imposing any prior carrier identification on $J$.

proof.text: Fix $B=(K,\theta)$ and abbreviate $\vartheta=\vartheta_{K,\theta}$. By the fixed-pair morphism condition [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], the counit $\widetilde F\widetilde G B\to B$, whose carrier is $\varepsilon_K$ by hypothesis, satisfies $$\varepsilon_K\circ F(\vartheta)\circ\beta_{GK}=\theta\circ P(\varepsilon_K).$$ Compose on the right with $\beta_{GK}^{-1}$, which exists by hypothesis, to obtain $$\varepsilon_K\circ F(\vartheta)=\theta\circ P(\varepsilon_K)\circ\beta_{GK}^{-1}:FQGK\longrightarrow K.$$ This uses no cancellation of $F$ or of $\varepsilon_K$.

proof.text: The candidate $G(\theta)\circ e_K:QGK\to GK$ has exactly the same counit composite. Indeed naturality of the original counit at $\theta:PK\to K$ and the given mate equation [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] give $$\begin{aligned}\varepsilon_K\circ F(G(\theta)\circ e_K)&=\varepsilon_K\circ FG(\theta)\circ F(e_K)\\&=\theta\circ\varepsilon_{PK}\circ F(e_K)\\&=\theta\circ P(\varepsilon_K)\circ\beta_{GK}^{-1}.\end{aligned}$$ All maps have source $FQGK$ and target $K$; in particular $\varepsilon_{PK}$, rather than $\varepsilon_K$, occurs before applying the mate equation.

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), adjunction maps and the equivalence of clauses (1)–(3); explicit fixed-pair calculation by Q48.

proof.text: Use the natural Hom bijection of $F\dashv G$ with $X=QGK$ and $Y=K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], its inverse is $b\mapsto\varepsilon_K\circ F(b)$, hence is injective. Steps 1 and 2 therefore imply $$\vartheta_{K,\theta}=G(\theta)\circ e_K.$$ The right side is invertible because $\theta$ and $e_K$ are isomorphisms and a functor sends an inverse to an inverse. Thus $\widetilde G(K,\theta)$ has precisely the asserted structure, with no extra equivalence hypothesis on $P$ or $Q$.

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), adjunction maps and the equivalence of clauses (1)–(3); explicit fixed-pair calculation by Q48.

proof.text: Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] in the categories $\mathcal C^Q$ and $\mathcal D^P$, with its $F=\widetilde F$, its first right adjoint $G=J$ with counit $\kappa$, and its second right adjoint $J=\widetilde G$ with the given lifted counit $\widetilde\varepsilon$. It gives a natural isomorphism $\alpha:J\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde G$, unique among counit-compatible natural transformations, characterized at $B=(K,\theta)$ by $$\widetilde\varepsilon_B\circ\widetilde F(\alpha_B)=\kappa_B.$$ This is uniqueness of the isomorphism itself, not merely of an isomorphism class; no carrier identification of $J$ has been used.

source.place: Transposes, Naturality, Inverse and Uniqueness, specialized to the fixed-pair categories.

proof.text: Apply the forgetful functor [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category] to the equation in step 4. It preserves composition, $\widetilde F$ acts by $F$ on carrier maps, and the carrier of $\widetilde\varepsilon_B$ is $\varepsilon_K$ by hypothesis. Therefore $$\varepsilon_K\circ F(\operatorname{For}(\alpha_B))=\operatorname{For}(\kappa_B).$$ Step 3 identifies the target of $\alpha_B$ as $(GK,G(\theta)e_K)$, so $\alpha_B$ is the required canonical isomorphism in $\mathcal C^Q$.

lean.statement: theorem fixedPair_rightAdjoint_comparison {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D] {Q : C ⥤ C} {P : D ⥤ D} {F : C ⥤ D} {G : D ⥤ C} (adj : F ⊣ G) (β : F ⋙ P ≅ Q ⋙ F) (e : G ⋙ Q ≅ P ⋙ G) (hMate : (mateEquiv adj adj (TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ β.inv)).natTrans = e.hom) (Gtilde : IsoAlgebra P ⥤ IsoAlgebra Q) (lifted : mapOfNatIso β ⊣ Gtilde) (hCarrier : Gtilde ⋙ forget Q = forget P ⋙ G) (hCounit : ∀ B : IsoAlgebra P, F.map ((eqToIso hCarrier).inv.app B) ≫ (lifted.counit.app B).hom.f = adj.counit.app B.carrier) : (∀ B : IsoAlgebra P, Q.map ((eqToIso hCarrier).inv.app B) ≫ (Gtilde.obj B).str.hom ≫ (eqToIso hCarrier).hom.app B = e.hom.app B.carrier ≫ G.map B.str.hom) ∧ (∀ (J : IsoAlgebra P ⥤ IsoAlgebra Q) (adjJ : mapOfNatIso β ⊣ J), ∃! α : J ≅ Gtilde, (∀ B : IsoAlgebra P, (mapOfNatIso β).map (α.hom.app B) ≫ lifted.counit.app B = adjJ.counit.app B) ∧ (∀ B : IsoAlgebra P, F.map ((α.hom.app B).hom.f ≫ (eqToIso hCarrier).hom.app B) ≫ adj.counit.app B.carrier = (adjJ.counit.app B).hom.f) ∧ (∀ B : IsoAlgebra P, Nonempty (J.obj B ≅ mk (G.obj B.carrier) (e.app B.carrier ≪≫ G.mapIso B.str))))
